title: Maintaining and Assessing Various Tissue and Cell Types of the Eye Using a Novel Pumpless Fluidics System
protocol: Design the experimental protocol.
Assign tissue placement in channels for baseline correction and test compound protocols.
Choose tissue or cell model to be placed in 3 of the 4 channels on each side of the MRM.
Arrange samples using one of two typical designs: different test compound protocols on each side or same protocol with different tissues on either side.
Adjust flow rate until change in lifetime ratio times 100 is approximately 3 for optimal OCR measurement.
Calculate volume of media to be added to each MRM insert at the beginning of the experiment.
Select test compounds to assess.
Determine the concentration to be tested for each compound.
Prepare stocks of test compounds in desired solvent such as water, DMSO, or ethanol.
Choose timing of injections so that the response reaches a steady state prior to adding subsequent agents.
Match timing of injections when repeating protocols to average multiple time courses.
Select fraction collection intervals from 1-60 min/sample based on expected changes in concentration.
Ensure adequate well volumes to avoid overflow during sampling interval.
Prepare Krebs-Ringer bicarbonate buffer the day before based on calculations from equation 1, typically 200 mL.
Incubate prepared buffer overnight in a 39 °C/5% CO2 incubator in T225 tissue culture flasks with no more than 90 mL in each flask.
Place the MRM and fluidics package onto the bench next to the instrument.
Attach TCAs to injection ports on both ends of the MRM so that the end of the tubing is positioned directly over the stir bar.
Attach gas inflow feed line and purge tubing assembly to the back and front vacant ports, respectively.
Place the MRM (with the tubing assemblies attached) into the MRM heater.
Position the four tubing assemblies into the grooves of the walls in the base of the enclosure (two on each side).
Secure the MRM between the clamps by tightening the two wheels on the detector stand.
Feed the longer test compound injection assembly through the tube guides on the side of the enclosure so the opening faces forward.
Clamp each closed test compound injection assembly.
Toggle the power strip to supply power to all electrical devices within the enclosure to the ON position.
Turn ON the stirrers to 70 rpm using the user interface to ensure smooth rotation.
Place the middle section of the enclosure on top of the base.
Connect the cable from the middle section of the enclosure to the cable from the electrical box.
Place the lid on the enclosure.
Start a timer for 30 min.
Use the TCA insertion tool to insert each of the 8 TCAs into the PCM holes by firmly pressing until the top of the tubing sleeve touches the surface circumscribing the holes in the PCM.
Completely insert one TCA before inserting the next one.
Transfer pre-equilibrated perifusate into the pre-heated MRM insert using a 50 mL pipette.
Gently dispense the liquid down the sides to avoid transfer of gas between the perifusate and the atmosphere.
Assemble the MRM/PCM to create a gas-tight seal.
Insert the resistance tubes from the bottom of the PCM into the MRM inserts, 4 on each side of the MRM Divider.
Position the PCM so that the tissue chambers can rest against the O2 detector once positioned.
Secure the PCM and PCM Support Brace with 6 screws using an electric screwdriver.
Secure the TCAs within the PCM support fins with an elastic band by stretching it around the fins at the level of the rubber gaskets.
Place the O2 Detector on the detector stand so that its face rests against the fins of the PCM.
Adjust the LED/photodetector pairs to line up with the O2-sensitive dye in the tissue chambers.
Loosen the set screws on the side of the O2 detector holder if necessary and adjust the lateral guides.
Place the lid on top of the Enclosure.
With the high-pressure valve fully secured and closed, open the gas tank valve by turning it counterclockwise.
Adjust the high-pressure regulator to a pressure of 10 psi using the knob on the regulator.
Pressurize the MRM by setting the low-pressure regulator to 1.0 psi.
Unclamp the purge tube to allow gas from the tank to replace air in the MRM headspace for 15 min.
Submerge the end of the purge tube into a beaker of water to confirm gas flow by observing bubbling.
Start the O2 detector as described in section 3.8 once gas flow is confirmed.
Turn the stirrer on at 70 rpm and leave running for the rest of the experiment.
Clamp the purge tubing assembly after an additional 15 min.
Lower the pressure on the low-pressure regulator to achieve the desired liquid flow rate (usually between about 0.5-0.7 psi).
Temporarily set the pressure to 0.3 psi if the tissue is loaded within 15 min of clamping and the flow rate exceeds 20 µL/min.
Activate the O2 detector software on the laptop by clicking on the icon labeled Oxygen Detector.
Confirm the correct COM port is selected in the program.
Unplug and plug the O2 detector to display the port number if needed.
Close and reopen the application if the COM port is unplugged during use.
Click Start then Record and save data in the backup folder.
Change the average value on the bottom left of the lifetime graph to 5.
After a minute, click Auto Scale when the first data point appears.
Position frits in tissue chambers by removing lid and middle sections of enclosure.
Push frit down with frit cue after perifusate rises above pre-positioned frit.
Ensure frit is positioned about 0.25 inch above bottom of tissue chamber.
Load tissue into the chamber once media level is 0.5 inch from top.
Harvest Retina or RPE-choroid-sclera as described in 6.
Use fine point forceps to gently place the tissue into each chamber, being careful not to fold the tissue.
Prevent liquid from the tissue chamber dripping onto the O2 sensor using a tissue wipe.
Observe tissue sinking toward and onto the frit.
Ensure trauma to the tissue is avoided by not leaving it in a bicarbonate-based buffer/media out of the incubator for more than 10 min.
Bathe the tissue in enough buffer/media (at least 1 mL/10 mg of tissue) to keep the tissue from becoming hypoxic.
Prevent exposure to air when handling the tissue.
Prepare RPE cells as described previously and in Supplementary File 1.
Passage cells using 0.25% trypsin-EDTA and seed on polyethylene terephthalate, track-etched filters at a minimum of 2.0 x 10^5 cells/cm².
Cut the membranes into three strips of equal width on the day of the experiment.
Load the membrane strips with forceps into the tissue chambers.
Remove outflow tubing assemblies from packaging.
Place the outflow tubing separator on the lip of the middle section of the enclosure so the adapters are inside.
Being careful not to push too hard, attach outflow tubing adapters onto the top of the tissue chambers TCAs.
Replace the middle enclosure component and reconnect the ambient temperature control cable.
Confirm that all components inside the enclosure are properly positioned as shown in Figure 8E.
Replace the lid of the enclosure.
Feed eight outflow tubes through the fraction collector guide arm.
Center the fraction collector relative to the right wall of the enclosure, with its left support resting against the edge of the enclosure wall.
On the laptop, click the UI shortcut and open the experimental info page.
Fill in the information on the experimental info page as required.
Click the Flow & Fraction Collector page on the top for setting parameters.
Select an integration time that balances accuracy and temporal resolution from the sample acquisition time drop-down menu.
If no outflow fractions will be collected, click Start and proceed to section 4.7.
Check the Collect fractions? box on either the experiment info page or the flow & fraction collector page.
Click Compute FC Settings after checking the collect fractions option.
Fill in the time of the first injection (time = 0), flow rate per channel, and time intervals for each sample.
Click Compute to verify the collection intervals.
Generate and start the process once the intervals are verified.
Weigh eight or fewer microcentrifuge tubes and record their weight if measuring individual channel flow rates is necessary.
Set the tube holder containing the pre-weighed microcentrifuge tubes on the plate carriage for flow rate measurement.
Click Measure Flow Rate Manually in the other utilities section to measure the flow rate.
Select the measurement duration.
Click Generate Template.
Close the window and click Start.
The fraction collector will collect fluid from the outflow tubes for the measurement duration.
The arm will return to its home position after collection.
Weigh the microfuge tubes after collection.
Calculate the flow rate using the difference in weight divided by the measurement duration (1 mg = 1 µL).
Once tissue and/or cells are loaded into the tissue chambers, allow the system to equilibrate for 90 min.
Establish a flat baseline of O2 consumption at which time the first test compound can be injected (considered as time = 0).
At 30 minutes prior to the first injection, enter the average last 3 FR per channel value into the injection page.
Enter the names of the compounds, desired concentrations, and injection times of the test compounds into the table in the UI on the Injection page.
Confirm the information displayed in the program including volumes in the MRM left at the time of the injections.
Confirm how much stock solution to inject to achieve the desired concentrations.
Calculate the required amounts of perifusate and stock solution using the injection table.
Dilute the test compound stock solution with perifusate to achieve a volume that is 5% of the MRM volume.
Load syringes containing the diluted test compound for at least 10 minutes in a CO2 incubator maintained between 37-40 °C.
Connect the syringe containing the test compound to the injection lines.
Unclamp the soft-walled tubing leading to the injection line and inject the test compound at approximately 3 mL/min.
Re-clamp the tubing on the injection line after injection, then remove the syringe.
Repeat the injection process for the other side of the MRM.
Prepare subsequent test compounds according to the UI injection page before injecting them.
At the end of every experiment, inject KCN (3 mM) to determine the inflow lifetime signal for each channel.
Click the Save button on the top left of the graphing window in the oxygen detector software.
Name the file and store it in the designated folder.
Click the Stop Recording button on the main window to save the backup file.
Click the Save profile button on the top left of the UI's general page.
Name the file and store it into the designated folder.
On the fraction & flow page of the UI, click the Tools drop down menu and then Save.
Keep or choose another name for the generated file and store where desired.
Dispose of fluidics assemblies containing KCN in a fume hood.
Pour media from MRM and FC waste tray into a waste container.
Rinse the MRM inserts and stir bars thoroughly with water.
Pour contents of the waste container (containing KCN) into a labeled chemical waste container for disposal by chemical safety.
Thoroughly clean the stir bars and forceps prior to the next experiment.
Autoclave the cleaned stir bars and forceps before reuse.
Open the data processor application on a Mac or PC computer.
Select the .csv data file generated by an experiment.
If similar to a previously analyzed experiment, select that settings file and click Next Step.
Otherwise just click Next Step to begin entering the experiment's settings.
Fill in the various settings of the experiment.
Select the reference time point directly before KCN went into effect using a slider or by typing the time value.
Click Calculate to generate OCR graphs according to equation 2.
Save the generated graphs as .pdf files by pressing the Export Graph button.
Graph OCR values either as absolute values or as a fraction of steady state values by checking corresponding boxes in edit settings.
If samples cannot be assayed immediately, place plates at 4 °C if assaying the next day, or freeze them for longer storage.
Thaw frozen samples at 4 °C to keep them cold.
Enter columns of data (one per channel) into a .csv file with time in min on the left and concentration on the right.
Upload the template using the link in the data processing program.
